name: earthquake
job: Rank 250 m Neighbourhoods by the chance that buildings were damaged, from a NISAR coherence time series (self-supervised GRU anomaly), coherence loss and statistically normalised backscatter change
user: Search-and-rescue and damage-assessment teams deciding where to look first

labels.source: Copernicus EMS EMSR884 building damage grades: EMSR884_AOI02_GRA_MONIT01_v2, EMSR884_AOI02_GRA_PRODUCT_v1, EMSR884_AOI12_GRA_MONIT01_v3, EMSR884_AOI12_GRA_MONIT02_v1, EMSR884_AOI12_GRA_PRODUCT_v2
labels.notes: Positive = any building graded Damaged or Destroyed; Neighbourhoods with only 'Possibly damaged' are left out; negatives are analysed areas with no graded building.

baseline.name: Mean coherence loss across the event (Yun et al. 2015 DPM)

model.name: Ensemble LightGBM + U-Net with isotonic calibration

extra_scores.name: Unsupervised: Stouffer fusion (GRU only: GCOV missing)

split: Spatial 5-fold cross-validation over 5 km blocks, 5 shifted layouts for LightGBM (235 damaged, 1552 undamaged Neighbourhoods); out-of-fold scores
limits: Labels cover only the Caraballeda coast and part of Caracas; elsewhere the map is an extrapolation
Copernicus graded damage from optical imagery: hidden damage is missed, so some negatives are wrong
40 m features and 250 m Neighbourhoods find damaged areas, not individual damaged buildings
One earthquake, one track (126 descending); coherence also falls for non-damage reasons (vegetation, rain, works)
PROVISIONAL NISAR products: re-run when VALIDATED granules exist
Probabilities are calibrated on the labelled strip only: use rank_pct / classes elsewhere (see the extrapolated flag)
Backscatter (GCOV) evidence was NOT used in this run
Fault size is constrained by the USGS moment (joint, not independent)
